title: Meso-Scale Particle Image Velocimetry Studies of Neurovascular Flows In Vitro
protocol: Design an inverse model of the desired tissue phantom using CAD software.
Print the model using a 3-D printer with ABS as the building material.
Mix the PDMS prepolymer base and curing agent in a 10:1 ratio (by weight).
Place the mixture in a vacuum desiccator for 60 min to degas and minimize bubble entrapment.
Use cyclic pressurization/depressurization to facilitate bubble rupture.
Mount the printed ABS mold on a glass slide using molding putty to seal the interface.
Carefully pour the PDMS mixture into the mold while trying to minimize bubble entrapment.
Lingering bubbles can be manually ruptured using a needle.
Cure the cast phantom at room temperature (25 °C) for at least 24 h.
Submerge the phantom in acetone and sonicate for at least 15 min, using powers up to 70 W.
Thoroughly rinse the phantom with isopropyl alcohol.
Thoroughly rinse the phantom with DI water to remove solvent residues.
Mix PDMS with acetone.
Rinse and dry the phantom sufficiently.
Capture an image of a critical feature within the phantom using an optical microscope under appropriate magnification.
Capture an image of a calibration reticle at the same magnification as the phantom feature.
Load both images into ImageJ software by dragging them onto the Toolbar.
Select the Line tool in ImageJ to draw a line along a known distance on the calibration reticle image.
In the Set Scale window, enter the length of the drawn line and its unit of measurement.
Check the Global box to apply this calibration factor to all open images.
Draw a line along a feature of interest in the phantom critical feature image using the Line tool.
Select Analyze > Measure from the ImageJ menu to measure the length of the line.
Compare the measured length with the expected value to confirm phantom fidelity.
Mix DI water and glycerol in a 60:40 ratio (by volume).
Add 1 mL of 2.5% w/v fluorescent polystyrene bead solution to the mock blood solution.
Homogenize the mixture on a magnetic stir plate at 400 rpm for 10 min.
Cut off the DC-end plug from the AC-to-DC adapter power source.
Strip the coating off the power and ground wires from the AC-to-DC adapter.
Connect the power and ground wires to the input terminal of the PWM voltage regulator.
Connect the power and ground wires from the pump's DC motor to the output terminal of the PWM voltage regulator.
Prepare 200 mL of mock blood solution.
Place tubing from the pump inlet to a beaker holding the mock blood solution.
Place tubing from the pump outlet to an empty beaker.
Select a desired duty cycle set point (0% - 100%).
Press the On button and start a timer.
Stop the timer once the pump has transferred the entire volume of mock blood solution.
Use this time to calculate the volumetric flow rate.
Repeat steps for at least five different duty cycle set points to establish a least-squares regression curve.
Determine the calibration ratio for the video imaging.
Place the PDMS phantom on the stage of the fluorescence microscope.
Connect the phantom to the gear pump and introduce the mock blood solution.
Set the pump motor controller for the desired flow rate based on the pump calibration curve.
Run the pump for 1 - 5 min prior to the experiment to ensure steady-state conditions.
Turn on the external lamp to illuminate the field of view.
Select an appropriate filter based on the excitation wavelength of the fluorescent beads.
Adjust the imaging focal plane to the vessel midplane.
Select the video recording parameters to optimize the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Key parameters include exposure time, frame rate, and gain.
Drag the saved AVI file onto the ImageJ window to import it.
Select the box marked Convert to Grayscale.
From the ImageJ menu, select Analyze > Generate Histogram (or press Ctrl + H) to generate a histogram of image pixel intensities.
Take note of the mean and standard deviation for the unprocessed image.
From the ImageJ menu, select Image > Adjust > Brightness and Contrast (or press Shift + Ctrl + H) to apply a brightness/contrast filter.
On the Brightness and Contrast menu, press the Set button to define the image limits.
Set the minimum value to be the mean value plus one standard deviation.
Set the maximum value to be the maximum intensity of the image.
Select Process > Noise > Despeckle from the ImageJ menu to reduce saturated pixels.
Apply Gaussian Blur with a radius of 1.5 using Process > Filters > Gaussian Blur to minimize artifacts.
Outline the region of interest (ROI) by clicking on the Polygon tool and then clicking on the image.
Remove sensor noise outside the ROI by selecting Edit > Clear Outside from the ImageJ menu.
Perform PIV calculation using a third-party PIV plug-in for ImageJ.
From the ImageJ menu, select Plugins > Macros > Run…
Navigate to the saved macro Supplemental Code 2.ijjm to cross-correlate successive image pairs.
Perform a cross-correlation of the intensity field within consecutive images to determine local displacement of tracer particles.
Conduct a two-step multipass evaluation with initial interrogation window sizes of 256 x 256 pixels and final interrogation window sizes of 128 x 128 pixels.
Perform a temporal average to further reduce the appearance of spurious vectors.
From the ImageJ menu, select Plugins > Macros > Run…
Navigate to the saved macro Supplemental Code 3.ijjm to validate the velocity fields via the normalized median test.
